source.title: Flatter, faster: scaling momentum for optimal speedup of SGD
source.authors: Aditya Cowsik; T. Can; Paolo Glorioso

record.file_problem: Full text is present and readable; it contains minor OCR and typesetting artifacts.
record.tranche_reason: Tests how a heavy-ball momentum scaling affects test performance and Hessian trace, using experiments different from the claim versions' specified tests.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own results on momentum scaling, test accuracy or error, and Hessian trace. It does not test random-label memorization, width, convolutional versus fully connected architectures, adaptive optimizers, batch size, dropout, magnitude-aware sharpness, or removing memorized examples.
record.test_reason: The study tests momentum scaling for SGD with label noise, which none of V1–V8 names. Its Hessian-trace results do not test V7's magnitude-scaled perturbation measure or generalization-gap rankings. Adaptive-optimizer comparisons appear only as background; Adam is used for projection without a comparative generalization test.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is substantially correct. More precisely, the authors propose 1 − β proportional to η^(2/3) for maximal acceleration of noise-induced motion near a manifold of training-loss minimizers, and report that this scaling also yields the best generalization in their ResNet18 experiment. The conclusion concerns this specialized regime rather than unrestricted training speed.
record.recipe_differences: Uses heavy-ball momentum with SGD and label noise, studying a learning-rate-dependent momentum scaling; the claim versions concern other interventions and measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: Momentum β changes the speed of test-accuracy improvement and the expected test error in the reported experiments; the authors report the optimum depends on the learning rate scaling.

fits_no_version.finding: In matrix sensing, the same intermediate momentum optimizes the speed of Hessian-trace reduction and expected-test-error improvement.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Momentum has an interior optimum for the speed of generalization in this matrix-sensing setup with SGD and label noise.

fits_no_version.finding: ResNet18 test accuracy improves fastest at intermediate momentum, with the fitted optimum following exponent 0.660 and C = 0.11 after the study's training and projection procedure.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Near an interpolating solution, learning-rate-dependent momentum scaling can accelerate test-accuracy improvement under SGD with label noise.

record.problems: The realistic-model evidence is reported for one ResNet18 CIFAR10 run and lacks stated uncertainty estimates. The matrix-sensing test-error comparison is described qualitatively, with no numerical values in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant outcomes were reported beyond R1 and R2.

untested.parts: Fixed random-label fitting versus natural-label generalization and chance-level random-label test accuracy; stochastic label corruption here does not supply this comparison.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected performance on matched image tasks and the contribution of local connectivity.
Comparative held-out performance of adaptive optimizers and SGD under limited or broader tuning.
Large versus small batches under matched epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Effects of adding or removing dropout and weight decay.
Magnitude-scaled weight-perturbation tolerance, its relationship to training–test gaps, and ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Retraining after removing examples selected by memorization influence versus random removal.

record.verdict_notes: The row states are cannot_determine relative to V1–V8; this does not dispute the reported momentum effects. Appendix A.4 adds FashionMNIST momentum-scaling evidence, but it also fits no listed version. Epoch-wise double descent in matrix sensing does not test V2's width-dependent claim.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance on natural labels.
Width beyond the interpolation threshold and its effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Adaptive optimizers compared with SGD or momentum SGD under the specified tuning conditions.
Large versus small batch sizes under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Dropout and weight decay effects on held-out error.
Magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing examples selected by memorization influence and measuring test accuracy.

rows.subject: U V matrix model
rows.operation_detail: Swept momentum hyperparameter β during SGD with label noise and measured expected test error and Hessian trace.
rows.measure: Expected test error; the paper states the same β is optimal for expected test error and Hessian trace.
rows.baseline: Other tested β values; exact reference value not stated.
rows.value: The same β is optimal for both the Hessian and the expected test error; increasing or decreasing β from this value slows down generalization.
rows.note: The text describes the relationship but does not give the optimal β or numerical test-error values.
rows.check: The reported momentum optimum is supported, but it establishes no listed version. Expected test error is the noise-free population loss, proportional to squared Frobenius reconstruction error; Hessian trace is not V7's magnitude-aware sharpness.

rows.subject: ResNet18
rows.operation_detail: Trained with SGD, label noise, and swept momentum β after initializing on the zero-loss manifold; projected back onto the manifold before measuring test accuracy.
rows.measure: Test accuracy during training and after projection; optimal-momentum scaling fit.
rows.baseline: Test accuracy before the label-noise training phase; numerical value not stated.
rows.value: Test accuracy increases over the baseline as the Hessian decreases; this happens most quickly for momentum matching the scaling law. The fitted exponent is γ∗ = 0.660 and C = 0.11.
rows.note: The reported scaling fit is textual; the paper gives no numerical test-accuracy values in the text.
rows.check: The accuracy improvement and fitted exponent are supported but establish no listed version. Clarify that initialization uses the expected loss under p = 0.2 label corruption, and final projection uses full-batch Adam at learning rate 0.0001. The fitted exponent and C are hyperparameter-selection results, not test-accuracy values.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
